doc.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014

title: Nas sampling 'Smiling Billy's Suite' for 'One Love'
summary: The biggest income surprise was Nas sampling a few bars of Heath's suite for Billy Higgins, featuring Stanley Cowell and Percy Heath, in 'One Love'.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: When you go to the mail every day, this is sort of a personal question, but what kind of income might you receive that could be a surprise to you, from things you’ve done?

Well I think the biggest surprise was when I was sampled by a rapper by the name of Nas, whose father, Olu Dara, was a trumpet player. And Nas sampled me and, you know, I got big checks from his composition that he calls “One Love.” But all he used was a few bars.

No. Of the composition. It was on a suite that I wrote for Billy Higgins called “Smiling Billy’s Suite.” And one part had Stanley Cowell playing the kalimba, the African thumb piano. And my brother Percy played on the bass. And that composition was the one that was sampled the most.
